les: Iemand om na op te kyk
kaps_punt: Weeklikse lees deur leerders: lees vir genot: Lees oor rolmodelle of suksesvolle mense/mense met selfvertroue.

items.bewering: Siya Kolisi het as klein seun op 'n growwe veld in Zwide rugby gespeel.
items.bron: AFP via The42 (10 Nov 2019): his first coach Eric Songwiqi describes 'a gravel sports field at Emsengeni primary school in Zwide township' and 'a rough, hard, gravel pitch'; his uncle Vukile Kolisi says he 'grew up playing rugby barefooted on rough, dusty pitches'. https://www.the42.ie/siya-kolisi-south-africa-rugby-world-cup-4885947-Nov2019/

items.bewering: Zwide is 'n township in die stad wat ons vandag Gqeberha noem.
items.bron: SAHO: 'born ... in Zwide Township in Port Elizabeth (PE), Eastern Cape' (https://www.sahistory.org.za/people/siyamthanda-kolisi). Port Elizabeth officially renamed Gqeberha in the Government Gazette of 23 Feb 2021 (TimesLIVE https://www.timeslive.co.za/news/south-africa/2021-02-23-it-is-official-port-elizabeth-has-a-new-name-gqeberha/; SAnews https://www.sanews.gov.za/south-africa/name-change-shakeup-eastern-cape). Zwide lies about 17 km north of the city centre, inside the metro.

items.bewering: Hy is in 1991 daar gebore en het by sy ouma grootgeword.
items.bron: SAHO: born 16 June 1991 in Zwide Township, 'raised by his paternal grandmother' (https://www.sahistory.org.za/people/siyamthanda-kolisi); Wikipedia: born 16 June 1991, Port Elizabeth, raised by his grandmother Nolulamile (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siya_Kolisi). Note: his autobiography says an aunt raised him after the grandmother died (SA Rugby Mag, https://www.sarugbymag.co.za/?p=132592); the lesson's sentence does not contradict that.

items.bewering: Daar was dikwels min kos in die huis en geen geld vir rugbyskoene nie.
items.bron: The Citizen long read: 'Going hungry was hardly a weird feeling'; his grandmother 'would clean kitchens just to scrape together enough money for the odd meal' (https://www.citizen.co.za/sport/rugby/long-read-the-incredible-journey-of-siya-kolisi/). AFP via The42, uncle Vukile Kolisi: at nine 'he would come home with his feet bleeding ... because he did not have rugby boots'.

items.bewering: Party aande was daar niks om te eet nie, en hy het honger gaan slaap.
items.bron: Big Issue SA: 'Growing up in Zwide ... Siya Kolisi often went to bed hungry' (https://www.bigissue.org.za/the-kolisis-mission-to-change-lives/); Kolisi in the Sunday Times, 3 Oct 2021, 'It's hard to explain hunger to people who've never experienced it'.

items.bewering: Siya het by African Bombers, 'n klub in sy eie buurt, leer rugby speel.
items.bron: SAHO: started rugby at seven at Emsengeni Primary 'when he joined the local rugby team, African Bombers Rugby Club'; SA Rugby Mag (autobiography excerpt): the Bombers were based at Dan Qeqe Stadium, a short walk from his home; The Herald 2016: the club 'where his rugby career began'. Note: his first rugby also happened at Emsengeni Primary School in Zwide; 'leer rugby speel' at the club is still supported.

items.bewering: Hy het as kind dikwels kaalvoet gespeel.
items.bron: AFP via The42 (10 Nov 2019), uncle Vukile Kolisi: 'Siya grew up playing rugby barefooted on rough, dusty pitches.' Only one family source carries the detail, but it is a named, on-record account reported by a news agency and nothing contradicts it.

items.bewering: Hy is later vir die provinsie se onder-twaalfspan gekies. Daardie span het by 'n groot toernooi in Mossel Bay gaan speel.
items.bron: The Citizen long read: he 'ended up being picked for Eastern Province's Under-12 B side for a provincial tournament in Mossel Bay' (https://www.citizen.co.za/sport/rugby/long-read-the-incredible-journey-of-siya-kolisi/); Wikipedia and Nelson Mandela University: at 12 he impressed scouts at a youth tournament in Mossel Bay (https://www.mandela.ac.za/Leadership-and-Governance/Council-Prestige-Awards/Siya-Kolisi-2018). Precision note, not a fault: the one source naming the team says it was the province's B side, so 'die provinsie se onder-twaalfspan' is true but slightly general; ''n onder-twaalfspan van die provinsie' would be exact.

items.bewering: Siya het daar goed gespeel. Daarna het Grey Junior, 'n skool in die stad, vir hom 'n beurs aangebied.
items.bron: Wikipedia and Nelson Mandela University: 'at age 12, he impressed talent scouts at a youth rugby tournament in Mossel Bay' and 'was offered a scholarship at Grey Junior in Port Elizabeth'. The Citizen: his play was 'compelling enough' for a full bursary; one account says it covered one year at Grey Junior and five at Grey High, and Kolisi told the Mail & Guardian (2012) it was 'a scholarship to Grey PE for my grade seven year'. Grey Junior is in Port Elizabeth/Gqeberha.

items.bewering: In sy nuwe klas het almal Engels gepraat, en hy het min daarvan verstaan. Hy moes die taal van die begin af leer en het aangehou rugby speel.
items.bron: SAHO: when he arrived at Grey Junior 'he could not speak a word of English'; a classmate taught him English in exchange for isiXhosa. The Citizen: 'he initially couldn't speak a word of English'. The Grey's own mission statement: English is the medium of instruction (https://www.greyhighschool.com/school-information/mission-and-vision/).

items.bewering: Sy ma is oorlede terwyl hy nog op skool was.
items.bron: Sources differ on the exact age: Wikipedia and The Citizen say he was 15, SAHO says 16, and News24 (2016) gives 2009, his final school year (he joined the Western Province academy at 18 in 2010). Every version puts her death while he was still at school, which is all the lesson claims.

items.bewering: Ná skool het hy vir 'n groot span in Kaapstad begin speel.
items.bron: SAHO: joined the Western Province Rugby Institute in 2010, debuted for the Stormers in 2012; Wikipedia: senior Western Province debut in the 2011 Vodacom Cup. Both are Cape Town teams (the academy itself sat in Stellenbosch).

items.bewering: In 2013 het hy sy eerste toetswedstryd vir die Springbokke gespeel.
items.bron: Wikipedia: 'made his national team debut as Springbok 851 on 15 June 2013 against Scotland'; SAHO: Test debut 2013 against Scotland in Nelspruit.

items.bewering: Toe hy drie-en-twintig was, het hy sy jonger suster en broer by hom ingeneem.
items.bron: News24 (4 Aug 2017, 'Be their hero'): he 'was just 23' when he went looking for the siblings, who were in state care. Wikipedia: half-siblings Liyema (sister) and Liphelo (brother) have been part of the household 'since 2014', after five years in orphanages and foster care. Rachel Kolisi's own account puts it when she was 24 and their son Nic was 3 months old (Nic born 2014 per Briefly, 4 Sep 2026), which is late 2014, when Siya was 23 (he turned 23 on 16 June 2014). Note: they are half-siblings; 'suster en broer' is the usual way to say it. Legal custody was reported later (City Press, 2016), but 'by hom ingeneem' claims only that they came to live with him.

items.bewering: In 2018 het die afrigter hom as kaptein van die Springbokke aangewys.
items.bron: CNN, 28 May 2018 and ESPN: coach Rassie Erasmus named him captain for the June 2018 series against England (https://africa.espn.com/rugby/story/_/id/23734740/springboks-rugby-captain-siya-kolisi-ready-lead-south-africa).

items.bewering: Hy was die eerste swart speler wat die span in 'n toetswedstryd gelei het.
items.bron: Wikipedia: 'the team's first black captain in its 126-year history'; SAHO: 'the first Black player to hold the role'. He led them against England at Ellis Park on 9 June 2018. Nuance checked: he had already captained briefly, as a stand-in during a 2017 Test, when Eben Etzebeth was injured, and reports call that too a first for a black player. So the superlative holds whichever occasion counts, and the sentence names no date that could be wrong.

items.bewering: In 2019 het hy sy knie lelik beseer. Siya het week ná week gewerk om weer behoorlik te kan hardloop.
items.bron: TimesLIVE, 30 May 2019: he injured his knee scoring a try against the Highlanders, was ruled out of the rest of Super Rugby, and chose six weeks in a brace instead of surgery, which the paper called 'a risky strategy' in 'a race against time' (https://www.timeslive.co.za/sport/rugby/2019-05-30-injured-siya-kolisi-in-race-against-time-to-be-fit-for-boks/). His comeback came in mid-August 2019 (TimesLIVE, 12 Aug 2019; IOL, 18 Aug 2019). 'Week ná week' fits roughly eleven weeks out.

items.bewering: Hy het betyds vir die Wêreldbeker herstel en die span Japan toe gelei.
items.bron: Business Day, 18 Aug 2019: 'Siya Kolisi is good to go for the World Cup, says Bok coach'. The 2019 Rugby World Cup was in Japan, and Kolisi captained South Africa there (Wikipedia; SAHO).

items.bewering: Die Springbokke het die eerste wedstryd teen Nieu-Seeland verloor.
items.bron: Pool B opener, Yokohama, 21 Sep 2019: New Zealand 23, South Africa 13 (Wikipedia 2019 RWC Pool B, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Rugby_World_Cup_Pool_B; Daily Dispatch 21 Sep 2019 'All Blacks hand Boks their first defeat of the RWC').

items.bewering: Daarna het hulle elke wedstryd gewen en tot in die eindstryd deurgedring. Daar het hulle Engeland geklop.
items.bron: Read together with the sentence before it. After the opening loss, South Africa beat Namibia, Italy (49-3) and Canada (66-7) in the pool, Japan in the quarter-final and Wales 19-16 in the semi-final, then England 32-12 in the final at Yokohama on 2 Nov 2019 (Wikipedia 2019 RWC knockout stage, https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Rugby_World_Cup_knockout_stage; Wikipedia 2019 RWC final). Typhoon Hagibis cancelled no South African match, so 'elke wedstryd' holds.

items.bewering: Siya het as kaptein die goue beker bo sy kop gelig.
items.bron: Wikipedia: he captained South Africa to the 32-12 win in the 2019 final. The Webb Ellis Cup is gilded silver (silver covered in gold): https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Webb_Ellis_Cup, World Rugby (https://www.world.rugby/news/31319). 'Goue beker' is a fair description of a cup that is gold on the outside.

items.bewering: Die span het daarna met die beker na groot stede getoer.
items.bron: SAnews 'Taste of victory' and AP/Fox News: the trophy tour ran from 7 November 2019, starting at the Union Buildings in Pretoria and going through Johannesburg and Soweto, Durban, East London, Port Elizabeth and Cape Town (https://www.sanews.gov.za/node/45755).

items.bewering: 'n Oop bus met die beker het stadig deur Zwide se strate gery. Siya het die beker terug na die buurt van sy kinderdae gebring.
items.bron: AFP via The42, 10 Nov 2019: Kolisi was 'holding the trophy as an open-top bus crawled through the streets of a Port Elizabeth township', and the article names it as Zwide. Daily Maverick, 10 Nov 2019: 'The Springbok bus could hardly move in Koyana Street as thousands of Zwide residents lined the streets' (https://www.dailymaverick.co.za/article/2019-11-10-huge-turnout-for-kolisi-as-boks-bring-webb-ellis-cup-home-to-pe/).

items.bewering: Hy het kort daarna 'n stigting begin wat gesinne met kos help.
items.bron: The Kolisi Foundation was launched in April 2020, about five months after the November 2019 tour, and was brought forward because of the Covid-19 lockdown. Its first work was food parcels and vouchers for families: Kolisi Foundation (https://kolisifoundation.org/kolisi-foundation-whats-in-store-for-2021/), Dispatch Live 18 Apr 2020 'Siya Kolisi helps out hungry Zwide residents', Wikipedia ('launched The Kolisi Foundation in 2020'). Note: it also works on other causes, such as gender-based violence and education, but the lesson's sentence names only one of its aims and does not claim it is the only one.

items.bewering: In 2023 het die Springbokke weer om die Wêreldbeker gespeel. Die eindstryd was in Frankryk, en hulle het dit gewen.
items.bron: World Rugby finals review: South Africa beat New Zealand 12-11 at the Stade de France (Saint-Denis, France) on 28 Oct 2023 (https://www.world.rugby/news/889564/rugby-world-cup-2023-finals-review); Wikipedia.

items.bewering: Siya het die goue beker daar vir die tweede keer bo sy kop gelig.
items.bron: World Rugby / Rugby World Cup: Kolisi 'becomes the second captain to lift the Webb Ellis Cup for the second time' (2019 and 2023). Wikipedia: he captained both finals. The lesson does not claim he was the first to do it twice (Richie McCaw was), so no superlative goes past what the sources say.

items.bewering: Parallel set: the 2019 and 2023 World Cup paragraphs, read together (as captain both times; 2019 in Japan, final against England; 2023 final in France; lifted the cup twice).
items.bron: Tested as a set against the sources above. Every contrast the two paragraphs draw is true: a different host and a different final opponent, captain both times, and a second lift in 2023. Nothing in the 2023 paragraph implies the opposite of something true. The lesson does not mention that South Africa also lost a pool match in 2023 (to Ireland), or that Kolisi recovered from another knee injury before the 2023 tournament. Leaving those out sets up no false contrast, because the 2019 'elke wedstryd gewen' claim is tied to 2019 alone.

items.bewering: beurs: Geld wat iemand anders vir jou skool of studie betaal.
items.bron: Wiktionary (Afrikaans/Dutch beurs): an allowance from a foundation or other benefactor for a set purpose, such as a study bursary (English equivalents bursary, scholarship, study allowance). It is accurate on its own and in the lesson, where Grey paid for his schooling.

items.bewering: toetswedstryd: 'n Groot wedstryd tussen die nasionale spanne van twee lande.
items.bron: Dictionary of South African English: 'an international match in any sport or game' (https://dsae.co.za/entry/test/e07120); Merriam-Webster: a game 'played between teams representing different countries'; Wikipedia, Test match (rugby union): an international game, usually between senior national teams. A small simplification that is acceptable at Grade 4: a few Tests involve a combined side such as the British and Irish Lions, which is not one country.

items.bewering: eindstryd: Die laaste wedstryd van 'n toernooi, tussen die twee spanne wat die wedstryde net daarvoor gewen het.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Final (competition): the match 'in which the winner of the entire event is decided'; in knockout competitions it is 'usually played between the winners of two semifinals', and it is 'usually, but not always, the last match' (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Final_(competition)). Oxford Learner's: the last of a series of games, in which the winner is decided. Accurate for knockout tournaments, which is the only kind in this lesson; read on its own it is a fair Grade 4 simplification.

items.bewering: stigting: 'n Groep wat opgerig is om ander mense te help.
items.bron: Wikipedia, Foundation (nonprofit): 'a type of nonprofit organization or charitable trust', 'often set up for charitable purposes', with public-benefit, humanitarian or cultural aims (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Foundation_(nonprofit)). The Kolisi Foundation itself was set up to help people with food relief (https://kolisifoundation.org/kolisi-foundation-whats-in-store-for-2021/). Read on its own, 'om ander mense te help' is a little narrower than the full sense (some foundations serve cultural or research aims, or fund other charities), but it is true for the usual charitable foundation and exactly true in this lesson. No Afrikaans dictionary entry could be reached online.

opsomming: All 31 items hold against news, archive and reference sources: 27 from the Siya Kolisi reading, including the parallel test of the two World Cups, and the four glossary entries; this covers his age (23) when he took in his half-siblings, the barefoot detail (from his uncle, reported by AFP), the open-top bus through Zwide and every first or second-time claim; the lesson has no analogies; one optional precision for a person: the only source naming his Mossel Bay team says it was Eastern Province's Under-12 B side, so 'die provinsie se onder-twaalfspan' is true but slightly general.
